title: Auth0 Essentials to self-hosted Keycloak
summary: Auth0 prices by monthly active users; Keycloak does not care how many you have. This is the escape with the steepest operational cost.

you_lose: Auth0's uptime record, on the one service where downtime locks every user out of everything
Anomaly detection, breached-password checks and bot protection out of the box
Rules, Actions and the extension marketplace
you_gain: MAU-independent pricing — the reason anyone considers this at 10,000+ users
Full OIDC and SAML with no feature gating behind an enterprise tier
Apache-2.0 licensing and a CNCF-adjacent governance model

caveats: This is the one on this site we are most cautious about. Identity is the worst thing to run badly: a botched Keycloak upgrade locks every user out of every application at once.
The 24-hour migration estimate is realistic only if you already understand OIDC. Double it if you do not.
Auth0 Essentials at $35/month is priced for up to 500 monthly active users. Below that ceiling Auth0 is very hard to beat, and this page will usually tell you to stay.
Budget for a staging Keycloak as well. The arithmetic here assumes one box; a serious deployment wants two.
